By the right-triangle definitions, \sin\theta=\frac{y}{r}, \cos\theta=\frac{x}{r}, \tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}, \csc\theta=\frac{r}{y}, \sec\theta=\frac{r}{x}, and \cot\theta=\frac{x}{y}. This expression asks for the cotangent of \theta, so the definition to use is \cot\theta=\frac{x}{y}.

With x=8, y=15, and r=17, \cot\theta=\frac{x}{y}=\frac{8}{15}.

Therefore \cot\left(\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{17}\right)\right)=\boxed{\frac{8}{15}}.
